parsed.explanation: Adult alone: federal layer dominates border/documents/custody: passport/visa sex-marker restrictions, secondary screening, permanent-fraud ineligibility risk, and reported confiscation/stranding. If detained, immigration/correction policies permit denial of hormones, forced psychiatric treatment, beatings, solitary, and sexual abuse. State law materially improves adult local facilities, public accommodations, hate-crime recourse and documents, but does not pre-empt federal entry screening or federal facilities/custody. Adult with trans minor faces added school bathroom/pronoun and athletics restrictions, national youth-care criminalisation and insurance threats, though state conversion-therapy ban and adult-low-risk assessment limit extension to adults. Score reflects high risk: no credible execution, but severe state-imposed discovery consequences and thin certainty.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passport/visa rules refuse M/F only and X marker for new applications; officers may refuse cases for document discrepancies, treat alleged misrepresentation as material fraud with lifetime ineligibility; travellers report blocked passports and stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; litigation and legal-aid guidance challenge passport restrictions; no state rule alters federal entry screening.
entry_documents.interaction: State public-accommodation protections do not cancel federal entry screening; home-passport mismatch can trigger denial or investigation.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Secondary immigration screening can lead to custody. Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopted trans-inmate conversion-style treatment and hormone removal.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No operative traveller-facing custody protection documented; some national orders enjoined, but not detention practices.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visa/document mismatch can move traveller into federal custody; state protections may not reach federal detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender; some other state/provinces criminalise facility use and one documented arrest/trespass.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province protects gender identity in public accommodations and has a court bathroom precedent; low-risk assessment says adult targeting unlikely.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protections cover private/state facilities; federal or federally funded facilities may still exclude; combined exposure remains.

care_services.exposure: National rules/EO frame youth care as abuse, bar reimbursement proposals, and corrections remove hormones; minors may face emergency care discrimination; hospital records subpoenaed.
care_services.protection: State bans conversion therapy for minors and civil-rights public accommodation protections; adult clinic care restrictions not documented in state.
care_services.interaction: Adult routine care likely protected locally, but minor care and federally funded health settings remain exposed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism language lists radically pro-transgender groups as hostile; fraud findings; official hostility and facility arrest in other state/provinces.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National/state hate-crime laws, panic-defence repeal, employment-discrimination ruling, and state public-accommodation enforcement apply in this state.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Protective local law enforcement contrasts with federal framing; a traveller may face local remedy but federal screening/hostility.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face school bathroom/pronoun restrictions, athletics exclusion, national youth-care criminalisation, and document scrutiny for guardian; family visits may expose status.
minors_guardians.protection: State prohibits conversion therapy for minors; low-risk assessment suggests youth policies unlikely to extend to adults, not minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian's state protections reduce adult public-space risk, but minor school/care exposure and federal entry remain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific trans-violence rates documented; national polls show majorities support assigned-sex documents; bathroom arrest occurred in another state/province.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime law and public-accommodation statute may support police response; city/local protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street-level response likely more protective than other jurisdictions, but federal facilities/border remain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unclear whether school bathroom policy reversed; passport restrictions live after court approval; custody remedies weak; state variation and federal preemption unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil liberties lawsuits, legal-aid FAQ, state civil-rights enforcement, and some enjoined national orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may work locally but cannot reliably prevent federal entry/facility/custody exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A, federal visa/passport rules can refuse travellers on sex-marker discrepancy and create stranding, with little pre-travel remedy. It is less engineered than a visitor conduct register and has court challenges, but permanent-fraud risk, confiscation reports, and severe immigration/correction custody push toward the same high-risk zone.

Lower than 0.45-A: unlike narrow administrative holds, this combined regime adds federal secondary screening, possible lifetime ineligibility, and documented custody abuse. State public-accommodation and hate-crime protections materially reduce adult street/facility exposure, so it sits just below elevated-risk rather than clearly in it.

Far lower than 0.75-C, which describes respectful border inspection, presentation-matching passports, brief detention with counsel and compensation. Here passport markers are restricted, secondary screening can escalate to federal custody with abuse, and state protections cannot offset federal entry screening or government-funded facility rules.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is split: protective state law for adults vs hostile federal travel, facilities, custody, and minor-care layer. An adult alone faces lower local discrimination risk, but if documents/name/presentation mismatch at borders or federal settings, discovery leads to refusal/stranding, fraud bars, and potential severe immigration custody. A trans minor adds school pronoun/bathroom restrictions and national youth-care criminalisation, with guardian still subject to federal entry. Court contests and legal-aid guidance make outcomes uncertain, not safe. Overall: high risk, not catastrophic; execution is not documented.
